mentl/cb6b4b5:
Morgan asked whether lambda should exist. The medium's own census
answered: of 515 lambda sites, 197 (38%) were `(x) => match x { … }` and
57 more a single tuple pattern in param position — half the corpus paying
a wrapper to reach a form the language already had, while SYNTAX conceded
the point in prose and the parser charged for it anyway.

`{ p => b, … }` IS a function now; `match` is that function applied; one
parse_match_arms serves both. The build was smaller than the design,
because the desugar and its inverse both already existed for ONE arm:
`((a, b)) => e` has parsed since birth as a one-param lambda whose body is
a one-arm match on its own param, and fmt already inverted it. So the
literal is that graph with N arms — nothing in types/infer/lower or the
projections changed. Governing Principle 1 decided the rest: if two
spellings are one graph, which reaches the page is the formatter's call,
so fmt PRODUCES the literal and the corpus conversion was one `mentl fmt`
rather than 254 edits. The wheel fell 61,338 -> 60,989 lines.

Two silent wrongs the probes found and closed, both predating the literal:
a brace body discarded its postfix application (`{ let g = inc; g }(1)`
ran to exit 0 with zero diagnostics), and a closure captured inside a
closure returned the CAPTURE (`let g = f((n) => n * 2); g(4)` answered 8,
`p(4)`) because both record mints parked the pointer in one shared
$state_tmp. LCall had carried the per-handle fix since #115; the mint is
the same class. Both are permanent fixtures, each seen RED first.

The anonymity census was re-founded in the same landing — after the sweep
it would have convicted a form carrying no param list at all — and
frontier's re-sugar leg was updated rather than obeyed: its invariant
(no minted name on the page) held harder, only the spelling moved.

SYNTAX's `.field` accessor is struck: measured not to parse, zero uses,
and refused on its merits — a field is not a decl, so it would be a third
way to reach a function v
mentl/cbaecfd:
Yesterday's entry called pipeline's record destructure correct by
accident. The site's own comment refutes that — it destructures all three
fields deliberately, and explains why: a full pattern was believed to pin
the record's real layout, and the class already had the wheel's own name,
trecordopen-wrong-field. Both sites followed that discipline.

The discipline does not hold, which is the sharper finding. A complete
pattern over an open row and a partial one are structurally identical to
the medium: in both, the receiver's judged type is exactly the pattern's
own fields plus an open tail. The failing repro projects
{ zeta: t39682@e0 | r39684@e2 }; pipeline's site projected
{ args: ..., body: ..., op_name: String | r367192@e17 }. Same shape.
Nothing distinguished a safe site from an unsafe one, so the practice was
an author's promise the graph could not check, and a caller passing one
extra field sorting before args would have read the wrong slot silently.

Both receivers now carry the record types types.mn already declared. The
rows close — the projection that showed the open tail reads
{ args: List(String), body: Node, op_name: String } — so the offsets
resolve from the full sorted field set and are a proof. The types existed
all along at their declarations; only the parameters were unannotated,
which is the Intent Boundary annotations are reserved for.

Emit fell 175 lines and peak RSS fell about 17MB. Resolving real offsets
is less code, which is the shape a Carried-Truth fix should have.

The class is untouched: any unannotated record parameter still guesses,
silently, while its rest half traps. Its ultimate form stays the open
fork, but the wheel no longer depends on the answer.

mentl/cb05b79:
Bool moves from primitive `TBool` to ADT `type Bool = False | True`
declared in std/prelude.ka. False=tag 0, True=tag 1 — matches WAT's
i32 truthiness so `(if cond ...)` works directly.

Substrate decisions landed:

  HEAP_BASE = 4096 — sentinel-vs-pointer threshold. Bump allocator
    starts at 1 MiB (1048576) so sentinels never collide with valid
    pointers. Documented in types.ka next to the Ty ADT.

  LMakeVariant emit branches on field count:
    nullary  → (i32.const tag_id), zero allocation
    fielded  → emit_alloc(4 + 4*N), tag at offset 0, fields at 4+4*i

  emit_match_arms classifies arm shape ONCE upfront:
    pure-nullary (mode 0) → direct sentinel compare, no offset load
    pure-fielded (mode 1) → load tag at offset 0, current behavior
    mixed (mode 2)        → HEAP_BASE threshold gate, then dispatch
                            to nullary or fielded cascade

  Threshold gate: (scrut < 4096) — sentinels in low range, pointers
    above. Mixed-variant types like `Maybe = Nothing | Just(a)`
    work without ambiguity. Wildcards/vars/lits appear in both
    branches since they always-match irrespective of shape.

TBool deleted from the Ty ADT. Every reference swept:
  - infer.ka: 7 sites (LitBool, IfExpr, BinOp comparison/boolean,
    UnaryOp Not, LVBool pattern, same_ground/chase_deep/free_in_ty/
    subst_ty enumeration arms)
  - lower.ka: LitBool → LMakeVariant(handle, b ? 1 : 0, []);
    lower_param_handles arm
  - parser.ka: TName("Bool", []) instead of TBool for "Bool" ident
  - graph.ka, mentl.ka, pipeline.ka, backends/wasm.ka: enumeration
    arms cleaned (TName already handles the branch correctly)
  - docs/rebuild/02-ty.md: spec reflects deleted TBool

Why HB now (not deferred):
  Mixed-variant discriminator is the substrate decision; HEAP_BASE
  is the answer; the call sites are bounded; Bool-as-ADT crystal-
  lizes the H3 thesis instead of leaving it aspirational. The
  earlier "deferral" was fluency-driven caution, not a real
  constraint

clob/cbcff27:
An adversarial pass over the manifesto found one blocker and several
overclaims, plus the load-bearing numbers had no committed artifact.

- Bet 7 threshold was sign-flipped: the metric is 'Spearman rho between
  lambda1 and held-out NLL' but the intended outcome (NLL falls as
  lambda1 rises) is a NEGATIVE correlation, so the pass 'rho >= 0.6'
  would have scored the WRONG outcome as success. Redefine the metric
  as rho between lambda1 and capability (= -NLL); rho >= 0.6 now reads
  correctly. This corrects a pre-registered threshold in a commit that
  reports no run judging it, per the doc's own discipline.
- eps-stability wording overstated: the reproduction shows lambda1
  swings ~26% non-monotonically across eps 1e-3..1e-5 (-1.49/-1.23/
  -1.55). Only the sign and regime are stable. Reword to claim regime
  stability (deeply contractive, horizon 0.6-0.8 tok), not a precise
  constant.
- KS-entropy identity now names its conditions (SRB measure; Ruelle's
  inequality in general; generating partition) instead of asserting a
  bare double equality -- a document held to 'no prayer' should state
  what Pesin needs.
- 'Forget is the only irreversible step' now distinguishes the
  reversible retain-inputs steps from the erasure Forget actually
  performs.
- Causal numbers updated to the horizon-aware merge: 25 clusters, 7
  modules, A/B 7.0494 -> 7.0273 (-0.31%); merge wording notes it honors
  the split horizon.

noodles/cb264e7:
Stations are pitch classes times 7 mod 12, and since 7 is its own
inverse the same multiplication maps both directions. Signatures are
stations signed past the F#/Gb seam; each mode's relative-major offset
is computed from SCALES itself rather than tabled, so the one scale
source stays the one source. keyDisplayName spells a key by which side
of the circle its signature lives on (Eb dorian, not D# dorian), and
degreeStepSemis gives the diatonic extension interval that makes one
7 pad come out maj7 on I and dominant on V. Verified across all 72
mode/key pairs, including the sector theorem - the six non-dim triads
of every mode land on stations H-1..H+1 - by .tmp/dbg-circle-theory.mjs.
